evals.prompt: We're starting a new Rust backend: a URL-shortener API plus an admin CLI, sharing domain logic. The plan is one crate with everything in main.rs, actix-web, Diesel, `Box<dyn Error>` everywhere, env config via lazy_static + dotenv, tests later, and deploy by copying the debug binary onto an Alpine VM. Team of two. Sanity-check this and propose the layout and stack.
evals.expected_output: An opinionated redesign: a Cargo virtual workspace (resolver 3, edition 2024, rust-toolchain.toml pin, [workspace.dependencies] + [workspace.lints] inherited by each member, committed Cargo.lock) with crates/<app>-core (domain newtypes, thiserror errors, no I/O), <app>-cli (clap derive, anyhow, testable run()), and <app>-api (axum 0.8 + tower-http + tracing, lib.rs exposing app(state) plus a thin main.rs). sqlx with compile-time checked query! macros, committed .sqlx/ and embedded migrations instead of Diesel; thiserror in libraries and anyhow in binaries instead of Box<dyn Error>; a typed Config parsed once from env with std instead of lazy_static/dotenv at runtime; tests from day one (unit, proptest, #[sqlx::test] against real Postgres); release builds with LTO in a cargo-chef Docker image on distroless (not a glibc binary on Alpine), Kamal 2 with a /up route and graceful SIGTERM shutdown. Short reasons for each swap and first commands.
assertions: Proposes a Cargo workspace with a shared core/domain library crate plus separate CLI and API binary crates
Mentions workspace-level dependency and lint inheritance ([workspace.dependencies] / [workspace.lints]) and/or an explicit resolver = "3" with edition 2024
Recommends thiserror for library errors and anyhow for binaries instead of Box<dyn Error>
Recommends axum (with tokio/tower) for the HTTP service, or justifies keeping actix-web
Recommends sqlx with compile-time checked queries and migrations, or justifies keeping Diesel
Replaces lazy_static/dotenv runtime config with a typed config struct read once at startup (and/or std LazyLock)
Flags shipping a debug build and a glibc binary on Alpine; recommends a release build and a distroless (or musl static) image
Includes testing from the start (unit/integration, property tests, or real-database tests)

evals.prompt: Review our Rust workspace at evals/files/flawed_workspace and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review. Critical/high: SQL built with format! (injection), the std Mutex guard `hits` held across .await in `product` (!Send, deadlock), std::thread::sleep and std::fs::read_to_string inside the async `report` handler, `/products/:name` route syntax that panics on axum 0.8, std::env::set_var at runtime (unsafe in 2024), hard-coded Postgres credentials, `unsafe { get_unchecked(0) }` without a SAFETY comment (and UB on empty input), the Alpine runtime with a glibc debug binary. Medium: virtual workspace without resolver, api crate not inheriting [workspace.lints], anyhow and expect/unwrap in the core library, regex = "*", no Cargo.lock, sqlx macros without .sqlx/, openssl dependency, debug build in Docker. Low: edition 2021, tokio full, lazy_static, async-trait, Arc<PgPool>, println! in the library, version pins not inherited, no rust-toolchain.toml/deny.toml, untuned release profile, root container. Concrete fixes with code.
assertions: Flags the SQL built with format! as SQL injection and recommends bind parameters or query! macros
Flags the std Mutex guard held across .await in the product handler
Flags std::thread::sleep and/or std::fs::read_to_string blocking inside async handlers
Flags the `/products/:name` route as axum 0.7 syntax that panics on axum 0.8 (use `/products/{name}`)
Flags the unsafe get_unchecked without a SAFETY comment (and/or that it is UB on empty input)
Flags the hard-coded database credentials and/or std::env::set_var
Flags the Dockerfile: debug build and/or glibc binary on Alpine
Flags workspace hygiene: missing resolver and/or the api crate not inheriting [workspace.lints]
Flags the core library using anyhow and/or panicking with unwrap/expect
Orders findings by severity

evals.expected_output: Explains that the std MutexGuard is held across `.await`, which makes the future !Send so axum rejects the handler; recommends #[axum::debug_handler] to surface the real error; fixes it by scoping the guard in a block (copying the value out) before awaiting, keeping std::sync::Mutex (faster, Tokio's own guidance) and reserving tokio::sync::Mutex for locks that must be held across await; optionally suggests an AtomicU64 for a plain counter. Shows corrected code.
assertions: Identifies the std MutexGuard held across .await as making the future !Send
Fixes it by dropping/scoping the guard before the .await (shows code)
Advises against switching to tokio::sync::Mutex everywhere, reserving it for locks held across await
Mentions #[axum::debug_handler] for a clearer error, or suggests AtomicU64 for a simple counter

evals.prompt: Add a 'tags' feature to our axum + sqlx short-link service (same layout as the reference: crates/acme-api with lib.rs, links.rs, error.rs, migrations). Users can attach tags to a link (POST /links/{code}/tags with a list of tag names) and list links by tag (GET /tags/{name}/links). Show the migration, the module, and tests.
evals.expected_output: A new migration (tags table with unique normalized name plus a link_tags join table with foreign keys and a composite primary key); a tags.rs module with a Router<AppState>, axum 0.8 `{param}` routes, request/response structs with serde (deny_unknown_fields), tag names validated via a newtype (reusing Slug-style parsing) in the core crate, handlers returning Result<_, ApiError> with `?`, sqlx query!/query_as! macros with bind parameters, the multi-row insert in a transaction (upsert tags with ON CONFLICT, then insert join rows), 404 for an unknown code; merged into app(); #[sqlx::test] HTTP tests via oneshot covering success, validation (422), and not found; a reminder to rerun cargo sqlx prepare --workspace.
assertions: Adds a SQL migration with a join table using foreign keys and a uniqueness constraint
Uses axum 0.8 path syntax (`/links/{code}/tags`, `/tags/{name}/links`), not `/:code`
Uses sqlx query!/query_as! macros (or bind parameters) and never format!-built SQL
Wraps the multi-statement write in a transaction
Validates tag names through a type/constructor rather than ad-hoc string checks in the handler
Returns errors via the ApiError type with ? (404 for unknown code, 422 for invalid input)
Includes #[sqlx::test] (or real-database) HTTP tests using the router
Mentions regenerating the .sqlx offline data (cargo sqlx prepare)
